Opal provides symmetric residual predictors and controlled comparisons with strong same-information references. Historical neural models reduce mean squared error over additivity by \NormanGain\% on Norman and \WesselsGain\% on Wessels, but their advantage over development-selected simple references is inconclusive or negative. Exposed development favors economical residual kernels, and increased pair coverage helps more than the tested increase in single coverage on a fixed Wessels validation population. Technical partitions reveal unstable residual estimates without establishing a biological accuracy ceiling. An independent D-SPIN procedure evaluation yields MSE \DspinCandidate{} versus \DspinReference{} for the source-selected reference, failing superiority; source uncertainty also fails under shift. Preserved continuations support narrow known-compound dose interpolation but no newly validated pair/state component. A subsequent finite model-series evaluation trains main-effect selection, symmetric cross-coordinate bilinear residuals, and nested residual-memory routing. Bilinear improvements over the stronger Base reference are below 0.1\% on both responsive primary panels; routing fails its promotion rule. Three upstream-method adaptations execute under disclosed input and protocol differences, without establishing native competitiveness. The release supplies reproducible comparative evidence and scoped simple references, while positive independent transfer, biological interaction recovery, and calibrated uncertainty remain unestablished.

The selected neural family and the selected simpler comparator are chosen separately on development error and fixed before final evaluation. Their comparison can therefore reject the neural structural claim even when the network beats additivity.

Positive alignment alone can therefore be driven by shared reference geometry and cannot establish useful prediction.

The verified PRESAGE archive contains semantic embeddings, splits and ranked DEG lists rather than the required expression matrices. We therefore separately download the scPerturb release of the Replogle K562 essential-gene CRISPRi screen \citep{replogle2022} and verify its publisher MD5. It contains 310,385 cells, 8,563 output genes and 2,057 single-target conditions. Of these, 2,002 targets map to the supplied GO dictionary. A seed-fixed 1,601/401 training/validation target split trains a 16-to-32-to-16 encoder for 200 updates against training-target response PCs. Its normalized validation-PC MSE is 0.87670, versus 0.88021 for an alpha-ten ridge and 0.90792 for the training mean. These are source-task development scores.
